extracted.intended_audience: young aspiring novelists / writers reading Trollope's reflections
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and aesthetic guidance for novelists (and some nonfiction writers) based on Trollope's reflections: what makes books readable, how to handle satire and characterization, and professional habits for sustained literary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all the needs a book has the chief need is that it be readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trollope emphasizes that pages which 'drag' lose readers; readability is primary. Anti-pattern: producing work that, though informative or diligent, is not pleasurable or easy to read ('the pages drag with me'). Aim for prose that holds the reader's interest rather than only conveying information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough research and immersion (nonfiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: I spared myself no trouble in inquiry, no trouble in seeing, and no trouble in listening. I thoroughly imbued my mind with the subject, and wrote with the simple intention of giving trustworthy information on the state of the Colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For travel or factual books, immerse yourself in the subject, inquire widely, observe, and listen. This labour produces 'trustworthy information' even if some inaccuracies remain. Anti-pattern: quick, superficial work that cannot claim to be trustworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and accuracy (nonfiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: With all these faults the book was a thoroughly honest book... Though there be inaccuracies -- those inaccuracies to which work quickly done must always be subject -- I think I did give much valuable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for honesty and transparent reporting of facts; acknowledge limitations. Accept that rapid work may contain inaccuracies, but honesty and good-faith effort matter. Guidance includes admitting possible crude opinions or errors rather than presenting overconfident falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire: effectiveness vs truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The book has the fault which is to be attributed to almost all satires... The accusations are exaggerated. The vices are coloured, so as to make effect rather than to represent truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire often exaggerates for effect, but that exaggeration can make the satirist 'dishonest' in representation. Be aware that energetic satire risks sacrificing accuracy; weigh effect against fidelity to truth. Anti-pattern: knowingly misrepresenting for theatrical effect without regard for truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity/coherence of distinct parts
rubrics_metrics.description: I almost doubt whether it be not impossible to have two absolutely distinct parts in a novel, and to imbue them both with interest. If they be distinct, the one will seem to be no more than padding to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid splitting a novel into two largely independent parts where one becomes padding. Ensure plot threads and parts are integrated so each contributes to the whole; otherwise readers will find one part extraneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus interest on main (compelling) characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The interest of the story lies among the wicked and foolish people... But Roger Carbury, Paul Montague, and Henrietta Carbury are uninteresting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make principal characters engaging and central to the novel's interest. Anti-pattern: including protagonists or arcs that feel bland or peripheral, thereby diminishing overall reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-appropriate thematic authenticity (example: Christmas stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Christmas story, in the proper sense, should be the ebullition of some mind anxious to instil others with a desire for Christmas religious thought, or Christmas festivities,--or, better still, with Christmas charity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing within a particular genre or occasion (e.g., Christmas stories), genuinely address the thematic core of that genre rather than producing formulaic or commercial pastiches. Anti-pattern: forcing a work to fit a seasonal commission without authentic thematic engagement ('the humbug implied by the nature of the order').

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausible, specifically-drawn characterization (political figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: This man should have rank, and intellect, and parliamentary habits, by which to bind him to the service of his country; and he should also have unblemished, unextinguishable, inexhaustible love of country. That virtue I attribute to our statesmen generally... He should be scrupulous, and, being scrupulous, weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create believable characters (here: a statesman) by supplying concrete, plausible attributes and internal contradictions (e.g., patriotism plus scruples leading to weakness). Use specific social/occupational habits to ground character. Anti-pattern: vague, generic traits without concrete habits or moral tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of characterization across works/series
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of describing has not been confined to one novel... I have, for many years past, been manufacturing within my own mind the characters of the man and his wife.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characters recur across multiple books, maintain internal continuity of their traits and history so readers can recognize and believe them. Beware of contradictory portrayals that undermine perceived character identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persevering diligence and daily practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Nulla dies sine lineâ. Let that be their motto. And let their work be to them as is his common work to the common labourer. No gigantic efforts will then be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate steady, regular writing rather than episodic 'giant' efforts. Consistency of labour ('gutta cavat lapidem') will overcome difficulties. Practical guidance: work regularly but not in unhealthy marathon sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional reliability and commercial obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is his business, and he will starve if he neglect it... So have I felt that, when anything in the shape of a novel was required, I was bound to produce it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should meet commissions and deadlines as a matter of professional duty, even when the work is distasteful. Anti-pattern: refusing or shirking paid commissions that support a writing career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity versus quality (value of perseverance)
rubrics_metrics.description: It will not, I am sure, be thought that, in making my boast as to quantity, I have endeavoured to lay claim to any literary excellence. That, in the writing of books, quantity without quality is a vice and a misfortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mistake prolific output for literary excellence; nevertheless, sustained labour and output are virtues for a working author. Balance diligence with attention to craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid padding; economize the narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: If they be distinct, the one will seem to be no more than padding to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim elements that serve only as padding; ensure each scene, subplot, or character advances theme, character, or plot. Anti-pattern: lengthy digressions or separate strands that add bulk without interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read widely and annotate to improve craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Of late years, putting aside the Latin classics, I have found my greatest pleasure in our old English dramatists... If I live a few years longer, I shall, I think, leave in my copies of these dramatists, down to the close of James I., written criticisms on every play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study older dramatists and other writers closely; annotate and critique plays/works to deepen understanding of plot and character. Use close reading of varied models to sharpen one's own writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity in gendered portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: I think that Plantagenet Palliser, Duke of Omnium, is a perfect gentleman. If he be not, then am I unable to describe a gentleman. She is by no means a perfect lady; but if she be not all over a woman, then am I not able to describe a woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to render gendered characters convincingly and fully; aim for portrayals that readers will accept as authentic representations of 'a gentleman' or 'a woman' within the cultural context of the work. Anti-pattern: creating characters that fail to embody convincing gendered identity (as perceived by the author).
